summary: Follow-up on the Dec 1st outage that impacted Elysium's inference traffic for ~40 minutes. We covered root-cause hypotheses (KV cache invalidation + autoscaler misconfiguration), immediate mitigations, and reliability improvements (canary policies, tighter autoscale thresholds, additional OOM detection). Elysium requested detailed logs and a remediation plan; Redwood agreed to reproduce the failure on Dedicated and provide a timeline.
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date/time: 2026-12-02 15:00 UTC
Duration: 47 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Hayes (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Mark Rivera (Elysium VP Eng), Anika Bose (Head of Platform), Liam Chen (SRE)

Summary: Quick sync to run through the incident follow-up, align on RCA next steps, and agree on mitigations and timeline. Transcription is automatic, some words may be off.

Topics: Incident timeline, root-cause hypotheses, short-term mitigations, longer-term reliability improvements, security/compliance asks, next steps

[00:00] Jordan Hayes: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'll keep this short we wanted to walk through the incident from last night and make sure we're aligned on next steps.
[00:18] Mark Rivera: Yeah thanks Jordan, appreciate it. Quick recap from our side, we saw a sudden spike in errors and latency around 22:12 PST, traffic dropped to about 20% of normal and then full recovery after ~40 minutes.
[00:33] Priya Nair: Right, from the logs we pulled it looks like a combination of KV cache invalidation plus an autoscaler thrash. The cache invalidation caused cold starts and some models spilled memory, which then triggered scale-down events, then scale-up flurry.
[00:50] Anika Bose: To be clear, we were on the Redwood Dedicated pool with the default autoscaler config, yes? We haven't customized thresholds yet.
[01:05] Jordan Hayes: Correct, Dedicated with default policy; you were also using prefix caching and a warmed-up KV cache but there was a TTL cascade when a config roll happened - the transcription on the original logs had a bunch of K M S references that were slightly garbled but it's KMS key rotation we saw.
[01:24] Liam Chen: We did have a key rotation event at 21:58 which coincided with a config push from our infra team. We suspected that some of the prefix cache entries were invalidated as a result.
[01:40] Priya Nair: That matches our hypothesis. When cache entries are invalidated it forces more KV loads to backend storage. In a Dedicated environment that can increase memory pressure on the inference nodes because more kv cache shards are repopulating and some models allocate larger KV caches.
[01:58] Mark Rivera: There was also an error rate spike that looked like OOMs on one of the GPU hosts, the SRE team saw CUDA OOM logs.
[02:12] Priya Nair: We captured those. It looks like model weight quantization + the cold KV refill pushed the process over memory. We need to verify kernel selection - sometimes the runtime picks a different kernel path under higher sequence lengths.
[02:31] Jordan Hayes: One thing to call out - there was a fallback policy misconfig where requests were routed to a slightly larger model variant rather than a smaller low-memory fallback. That increased token cost and memory footprint. We'll include that in the RCA.
[02:50] Anika Bose: Ok so immediate questions from our leadership: was customer data at risk? We need clarity for compliance.
[03:02] Jordan Hayes: Short answer: no evidence of data exfiltration. The logs we have show internal service failures and retries. We will provide a SOC2-ready artifact and the audit logs showing access patterns.
[03:18] Mark Rivera: We'll need the audit logs and a signed statement for our legal team - can you include time-synced logs across load balancer, dedicated pool, and vault?
[03:30] Jordan Hayes: Yes, action item for me to assemble those.
[03:35] Priya Nair: From a technical mitigation standpoint, short-term we recommend: 1) pin model variants to avoid automatic fallback to larger variants, 2) tighten autoscaler thresholds (higher cool-down), 3) disable aggressive KMS-driven config reloads during business hours, 4) add an early OOM detector that drains traffic from an affected host before it fails.
[04:02] Liam Chen: Sounds good. For autoscaler, the thing we saw was a scale-down too aggressive for ephemeral memory pressure - the cool-down of 60s was too short.
[04:15] Priya Nair: Exactly, bump to 300s for scale-down and implement a smoothing window. Also enable continuous batching backpressure so we don't oversubscribe GPU memory during KV refill.
[04:30] Mark Rivera: For the longer term what do you recommend? Canary rollouts? More aggressive canaries?
[04:38] Jordan Hayes: Yes, canary by route + model variant, and a staged prefix cache warm-up on scale events. Also we can provide a config that pins quantization profile - quantized weights use less memory but sometimes different kernels; we should test in a staging Dedicated cluster.
[04:57] Anika Bose: Can Redwood run a repro for us? We need to see the exact sequence that leads to OOM so we can build our mitigations into our deploy process.
[05:06] Priya Nair: We'll run a targeted repro on a Dedicated node with the same model and sequence length distribution. We'll capture nvprof traces, kernel selection logs, and memory footprints.
[05:18] Liam Chen: Also please include autoscaler event traces and the routing decisions. We hit a fallback policy which surprised us.
[05:27] Jordan Hayes: We'll include routing trace and the timestamped decisions.
[05:31] Mark Rivera: On the compliance side, timeline for logs and the SOC2 artifact?
[05:37] Jordan Hayes: I can get the initial package to you by 2026-12-04 and the SOC2-ready artifact by the end of the week if needed.
[05:45] Anika Bose: That should satisfy legal for now. We may ask for a call with your security team after they review.
[05:52] Priya Nair: Noted; we can loop in our security lead if you want.
[05:57] Mark Rivera: For the repro, what do you need from our side?
[06:02] Priya Nair: Deployment config, the exact model version, sequence length histograms for the traffic window, and the autoscaler config. Ideally access to a snapshot of the prefix cache or at least the keys that were present before 21:58.
[06:18] Liam Chen: We'll share those by 2026-12-05.
[06:22] Jordan Hayes: Great. Next, reliability improvements: we'll propose a set of three mitigations you can opt into - short term (autoscale + pinning), medium term (canary + staged cache warm-up), long term (model-level quality monitoring and automatic fallback lints).
[06:43] Anika Bose: Also request that latency and cost dashboards show per-route breakdowns for the impacted model, so we can detect anomalies earlier.
[06:51] Jordan Hayes: Redwood Console can show token-level breakout, we'll enable a per-route dashboard and set alerts on abnormal token cost and tail latency.
[07:00] Mark Rivera: One more ask: we have a regulation that requires customer data not leave specific EU region; can you confirm whether any of the fallback routing went through other regions?
[07:10] Priya Nair: From our preliminary traces, routing stayed inside the EU region for that cluster. We'll include the geo-routing confirmation in the logs we send.
[07:20] Liam Chen: Perfect. On postmortem format, we'd like Redwood's RCA bullets and proposed mitigation timeline in a shareable doc.
[07:28] Jordan Hayes: We'll produce an RCA doc with timeline, root causes, evidence, and recommended mitigations - aim to have a draft by 2026-12-06.
[07:36] Mark Rivera: Sounds good. Any blockers on your side?
[07:40] Priya Nair: No blockers; main item is reproducing OOM which may take a couple days to iterate, but we will prioritize.
[07:48] Jordan Hayes: Ok let's capture the action items - I'll send calendar invite for the 2026-12-09 remediation touchpoint.
[07:57] Anika Bose: Thanks everyone.
[08:00] Mark Rivera: Appreciate the quick follow-up.
[08:04] [meeting end]

Notes: Transcript has occasional mis-transcriptions of product names (e.g., "KV cache" shown as "K V cache", "KMS" as "K M S"). References to logs and artifacts will be provided as links (S3 or secure share) rather than pasted here.
